paper.title: Safe Language Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Introduces safe identification and generation from jointly presented target and harmful languages, reduces safe generation to language identification, proves difference-emptiness and oracle impossibility results, and gives a positive theorem when every target-harmful difference is infinite.

formalization_scope.summary: All five numbered theorems have kernel-checked semantic content. Theorems 3.1, 5.1, and 6.2 use explicit source repairs; Theorem 6.1 is full for the explicit conventional representation by pairs of total Boolean partial-recursive codes; Theorem 6.3 is fully represented. The printed Corollary 6.1 reduction is formally shown to collapse under Definition 2 and the corollary remains open as stated.
specializations: Countable language collections are represented by explicit Nat-indexed families, preserving order and repetitions.
Theorem 3.1 replaces the undefined random insertion operation by a fixed candidate family in which every relevant safe difference is represented extensionally.
Theorem 5.1 replaces repeated finite generator runs by prefixes of fixed infinite labeled presentations.
Theorem 6.1 represents an input by a pair of Mathlib partial-recursive program codes, with a validity promise that both codes are total Boolean deciders for infinite languages.
The development is deterministic and semantic except for the concrete partial-recursive noncomputability reduction; it claims no extracted general algorithm or runtime bound.
gaps: Definition 1 does not specify a probability law, quantifier over insertion positions, or the learner's information about the random location.

The printed Corollary 6.1 reduction distinguishes empty from singleton differences although Definition 2 requires eventual bottom in both cases; convergence also supplies no computable stabilization bound.
The source does not specify a machine representation for arbitrary pairs of infinite decidable languages in Theorem 6.1.
Theorem 6.2's printed proof assumes but does not construct families satisfying Property P-star and describes future non-occurrence as observable.
No independent human source-correspondence audit is claimed.

audit_refs.scope: AI-assisted comparison of all five numbered theorems, Corollary 6.1, and Definitions 1--3 against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v2 PDF; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the P18 claim-linked endpoints.

exclusions: Definitions 1--3 and the unnumbered Section 7 observation are mapped in the PaperMap rather than assigned independent registry cards.
Algorithms, phase invariants, computability helpers, and proof-only diagnostics are linked through their headline claims rather than carded separately.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means every numbered theorem and corollary in arXiv v2 has a card; it does not mean every source claim is proved literally. Each card preserves its repair, specialization, or gap.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: The five source-numbered Results wrappers, the Theorem 6.1 restricted-hard-subclass and representation-transport wrappers, and the Corollary 6.1 collapse diagnostic.
exclusions: Paper-specific model definitions and internal construction lemmas are documented in the PaperMap but are not separate claim-linked endpoints.
Canonical proof declarations remain in their source modules behind the stable Results facade.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the eight selected claim-linked declarations, not every declaration below the P18 umbrella.

claims.title: Safe language identification is impossible
claims.statement_summary: Every safe identifier fails on some countable universe, pair of countable target and harmful collections, and labeled presentation.

source_assessment.notes: Definition 1's random insertion is under-specified. The fixed-family deterministic theorem proved in Lean isolates the strongest precise content supported by the phase argument.

formalization.notes: Lean proves a precise stronger fixed-family deterministic impossibility rather than inventing probabilistic semantics for the undefined insertion instruction.

lean_links.notes: Every relevant difference is already represented in the fixed family, and the exact tagged ranges are proved.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the repaired Theorem 3.1 Results wrapper.

claims.title: Safe generation is at least as hard as language identification
claims.statement_summary: A safe generator for every pair in the vertically padded copy of an arbitrary indexed family yields a positive-data identifier for the original family.

source_assessment.notes: The printed Algorithm 1 rebuilds finite generator inputs at each outer time, so the safe generator's fixed-run limit guarantee does not apply. The repaired construction uses exact prefixes of one fixed run per candidate.

formalization.notes: The repaired semantic reduction handles repeated family indices and proves every simulated call is a prefix of its canonical infinite run.

lean_links.notes: This is not an extracted membership-oracle implementation or a runtime theorem.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the repaired Theorem 5.1 Results wrapper.

claims.title: Difference emptiness is undecidable
claims.statement_summary: Deciding whether the difference of two infinite decidable languages is empty is undecidable.

source_assessment.notes: The mathematical reduction is valid, but the source does not specify how arbitrary pairs of decidable languages are represented as machine inputs.

formalization.notes: Lean chooses the conventional pair-of-partial-recursive-codes representation, proves undecidability over its entire valid promise domain, and also exposes the hard subclass and a transport theorem for other representations.

components.summary: Represent each input language by a partial-recursive program code promised to halt everywhere with a Boolean output and to accept an infinite set; every computable predicate is proved to admit such a code.
Construct uniformly decidable infinite language pairs from program codes and reduce nonhalting to difference emptiness.
Transport noncomputability to any Primcodable pair representation admitting a computable correctness-preserving embedding of the hard subclass.

lean_links.notes: The source leaves the finite representation implicit; Lean selects a conventional complete program-code representation and states validity as a promise.
This is the hard subclass compiled into the conventional pair-of-codes promise domain by the main theorem.
This remains useful for transporting the lower bound to alternative concrete encodings.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for the conventional machine-code Theorem 6.1, its restricted hard subclass, and the representation-transport wrapper.

claims.title: Identifiability alone does not make safe generation possible
claims.statement_summary: There are identifiable target and harmful collections for which no safe generator exists unless difference emptiness is decidable.

source_assessment.notes: The displayed empty-versus-singleton halting reduction cannot derive the corollary because Definition 2 requires eventual bottom for both finite differences, and an eventual guarantee has no computable stabilization bound.

formalization.notes: Lean formalizes and refutes the sufficiency of the printed reduction but does not claim that the corollary itself is false.

lean_links.notes: The declaration refutes the proof route, not the standalone existential corollary.

relations.notes: The source presents Corollary 6.1 as a consequence of the difference-emptiness reduction.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the printed Corollary 6.1 collapse diagnostic.

claims.title: A set-difference oracle alone does not make safe generation possible
claims.statement_summary: Some countable indexed families of infinite languages admit no safe generator even when the learner has an exact set-difference emptiness oracle.

source_assessment.notes: The source assumes but does not construct collections satisfying Property P-star and describes future non-occurrence as observable. Lean proves the existential theorem by a different explicit-family reduction.

formalization.notes: The corrected proof is stronger than needed: every oracle algorithm fails after specialization to every correct extensional oracle on the explicit padded family.

lean_links.notes: The proof composes repaired Theorem 5.1 with P28's explicit non-identifiable punctured family.

relations.notes: The corrected Lean proof derives safe-generation impossibility from the repaired identification reduction.
The repaired theorem vertically pads the P28 punctured family whose failure of text identification supplies the contradiction.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the corrected oracle-facing Theorem 6.2 wrapper.

claims.title: Safe generation with guaranteed infinite differences
claims.statement_summary: Every pair of explicitly indexed language families whose target-harmful cross-differences are all infinite admits a safe generator in the limit on every labeled presentation.

source_assessment.notes: Lean makes the finite-scope target criticality and harmful-candidate containment arguments explicit.

formalization.notes: The finite-history generator and complete eventual correctness proof are formalized at the source's semantic indexed-family interface.

lean_links.notes: Every cross-difference is assumed infinite, so the generator never needs the bottom branch.
